sources.name: Permanent time observation in the United States - Wiki

_: California authorized changes to daylight saving time in 2018, but attempts to adopt permanent DST failed in 2020 and 2022, while a 2023 proposal instead seeks to establish permanent standard time.
New York has multiple proposed options under consideration (permanent daylight saving time, Atlantic Time, or permanent standard time), but none have been enacted and the proposals remain pending.
Georgia passed legislation for permanent daylight saving time, while a separate proposal for permanent standard time failed.

Michigan has no active attempt to adopt permanent daylight saving time, but any change would require multiple neighboring states (including WI, IL, IN, OH, and PA) to also adopt year-round DST before it could take effect.
Washington has a planned bill proposing permanent standard time, but it is still pending and has not been enacted.
Arizona has observed permanent standard time since 1969 and therefore has not pursued or needed legislation to adopt permanent daylight saving time.
Massachusetts has proposed a shift to Atlantic Standard Time as a compromise alternative to both permanent daylight saving time and permanent standard time, but it has not been enacted.
The change would only take effect if federal law allows permanent DST and at least four additional Mountain Time states adopt the same policy.
Oregon proposed a regional plan for permanent time, but a permanent standard time bill failed in 2024 and any implementation depends on California and Washington also adopting the same system.
Utah has proposed permanent daylight saving time, but it has not been enacted and would only take effect if at least four of the listed western states also adopt permanent DST.
Idaho has partially approved permanent daylight saving time contingent on neighboring states, but broader implementation has not fully passed.
Hawaii has observed permanent standard time since 1967 and has not pursued legislation to adopt daylight saving time.
Maine has proposed legislation for permanent daylight saving time, but it only takes effect if all U.S. Eastern Time states and Washington D.C. adopt the same change.

Montana has proposed permanent daylight saving time, but it would only take effect if at least three neighboring states (Idaho, North Dakota, South Dakota, Utah, or Wyoming) also adopt permanent DST; the proposal has not been enacted.
Delaware passed legislation for permanent standard time, but it only takes effect if neighboring states (Pennsylvania, New Jersey, and Maryland) adopt the same change.
Wyoming has proposed permanent daylight saving time, but it has not been enacted and would only take effect if at least three of the listed neighboring states also adopt permanent DST.
